justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: Fraud Scoring Engine scores transactions (R-01), Case Management Backend supports analyst reviews (R-02), and Model/Rule Manager paired with Distribution Publisher enables zero-downtime model and rule deployment (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Low latency (sub-50ms at 3k rps) is targeted via Go with embedded ONNX runtime, ElastiCache Redis, and asynchronous Kafka auditing via MSK. However, Edge Tokenizer & Sanitizer running as synchronous AWS Lambda in the inline path risks cold starts and latency jitter.
justifications.compatibility: Compatibility is well defined with Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems via REST/gRPC, Card Networks / Tokenization Providers via mTLS, and compliance with parquet/Athena formats for external regulatory consumption.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are supported via Case API Router with OIDC/MFA; Data Scientists interact with Model/Rule Manager; Regulatory Auditors query audit logs via Athena. A dedicated analyst front-end UI container is omitted (only backend API is specified).
justifications.reliability: Amazon MSK Serverless, Aurora Serverless, and Fargate offer good availability. However, requirement R-07 (payments must not be blocked for >1 min if scoring is unavailable) lacks an explicit circuit breaker, fail-open mechanism, or bypass fallback.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance is thoroughly addressed: Edge Tokenizer & Sanitizer strips PANs, KMS Customer Managed Keys encrypt data at rest, S3 Object Lock enforces WORM for 7-year audit retention, and pgaudit/TLS 1.3 are implemented throughout.
justifications.maintainability: Responsibilities are cleanly decoupled across modular services (Scoring Engine, Case Management Backend, Model/Rule Manager). Small footprint on AWS managed/serverless services (Fargate, MSK, Aurora) fits the small 3-engineer operational constraint well.
justifications.portability: Core scoring, case management, and rule managers are containerized on ECS Fargate. The architecture relies extensively on proprietary AWS services (Athena, RDS Proxy, MSK Serverless), but properly satisfies the AWS eu-west-1 target requirement.

PERF-01.justification: Go-based engine with embedded ONNX runtime, Redis feature store, and async audit queuing natively supports sub-50ms P99 latency. However, synchronous Lambda edge sanitization introduces latency and cold start risks at 3,000 req/s.
sensitivity_points: Synchronous Lambda invocation latency on edge tokenization path.
In-memory ONNX model evaluation speed under concurrent load.
tradeoffs: Edge tokenization ensures PCI boundary isolation at the cost of invocation latency.

PERF-02.justification: Complete separation of scoring and case management workloads across isolated containers and datastores (Redis vs Aurora via RDS Proxy) ensures intensive analyst queue queries do not impact scoring latency.
sensitivity_points: Isolation of database connection pools between transactional and scoring paths.
tradeoffs: Dedicated Aurora and RDS Proxy infrastructure adds cost but isolates operational query traffic.

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture lacks an explicit fallback mechanism, circuit breaker, or stand-in rules engine in API Gateway to issue default decisions and record fallback audit trails if the scoring engine crashes.
sensitivity_points: API Gateway circuit breaker and default fallback routing policies.
tradeoffs: Failing open preserves payment availability but increases short-term fraud exposure.

AVAIL-02.justification: The Fraud Scoring Engine uses an embedded BadgerDB buffered dispatcher and MSK Serverless to decouple scoring from persistence, preserving all audit records during downstream slow-downs without degrading scoring latency.
sensitivity_points: Local BadgerDB disk capacity and flushing rate during MSK ingestion degradation.
tradeoffs: Local disk buffering adds task-level state but prevents data loss during broker outages.

MOD-01.justification: The Model/Rule Manager validates models, stores versioned artifacts, and notifies scoring engine instances via Kafka, allowing hot-reloads within embedded ONNX runtimes without downtime or lost version references.
sensitivity_points: Atomic model switching in memory without dropping in-flight scoring requests.
tradeoffs: Embedded runtime reloading increases memory overhead compared to external model servers.

MOD-02.justification: Rules updates are broadcast dynamically through MSK to the scoring engine, and the Explainability Engine calculates contribution scores and rule outputs directly on each decision without downtime.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic rule evaluation efficiency and rule compilation validation.
tradeoffs: In-process rule compilation avoids network hops but limits compute isolation.

SEC-01.justification: Edge tokenization removes clear-text PAN before internal storage, preventing analyst PAN access. However, the architecture defines no SIEM, behavioral analytics, or alerting mechanism to detect compromised accounts within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Sanitization consistency and lack of automated anomaly detection for analyst access.
tradeoffs: Tokenization reduces PCI audit scope but adds pre-scoring processing overhead.

SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode guarantees 7-year WORM retention with KMS encryption. However, lifecycle transition to Glacier Flexible Archive requires restoring archived objects prior to Athena querying, which requires extra orchestration within one day.
sensitivity_points: Glacier retrieval job latency and lifecycle expiration configurations.
tradeoffs: Archiving to Glacier cuts long-term storage costs but delays Athena ad-hoc query readiness.
